title: Parahippus is a divergent offshoot, not on the direct line to Equus

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Parahippus is a divergent offshoot, not on the direct line to Equus

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Because the skull of Parahippus fits the interpolated transformation series from Eohippus to Equus poorly, Parahippus is not in the direct line of descent but represents a divergent branch of the Equidae.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. XVII: On the Theory of Transformations, or the Comparison of Related Forms

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: In short, though some writers have placed _Parahippus_ in the direct line of descent between _Equus_ and _Eohippus_, we see at once that there is no place for it there, and that it must, accordingly, represent a somewhat divergent branch or offshoot of the Equidae.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter XVII, “On the Theory of Transformations, or the Comparison of Related Forms”; topic “Interpolated intermediates in horse evolution”. Scope: phylogeny of fossil Equidae

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch17-15: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.94

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The phylogenetic prediction is explicit and can be tested with extensive independent fossil evidence and modern methods. Missing fossil data affect certainty but do not prevent a strong resolution of branch placement.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Test Parahippus placement using public morphological and molecularly calibrated total-evidence equid phylogenies, independently of its fit to a skull transformation. Topological support for or against direct ancestry resolves the historical inference.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Direct ancestry is harder to establish than sister-group placement.

Fossil character matrices contain missing data.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Parahippus skulls and equid phylogenies exist in the literature and, unevenly, as scans. The logical step from 'fits the picture poorly' to 'not on the direct line' needs independent characters, which only partly exist for an extinct genus. Current material can test the geometric half and leaves the phylogenetic conclusion underdetermined.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Place Parahippus on the same Hyracotherium-to-Equus morph and on a cladogram of equids built from characters other than the interpolated skull warp. The claim is supported if Parahippus is both a poor geometric fit and sits off the Equus stem; a good fit, or a stem position despite a poor fit, would separate the geometric evidence from the phylogenetic conclusion.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
A poor fit to a linear warp can reflect age, sex or crushing rather than a side branch.

Equid phylogeny is morphological, so the tree and the skull transformation share character evidence.
